request.deadline: contract year covering 2026-2027; architecture assessment by Q3 2027; hard-fork compatible releases at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork
deliverables: Protocol maintenance including node upgrades, wallet backend updates, hard fork readiness, platform support, release engineering, security/dependency maintenance, and signed releases
Keystone and Flex hardware wallet support plus newer hardware wallet models as they emerge during the contract period
CIP-30 dApp connector implementation within Daedalus with documentation and interoperability verification
Japanese localisation and Japanese-language user support alongside ongoing English user support
Architecture assessment covering current state, options, resource estimates, and recommendation
request.recipient: Se7en Labs, Inc. through Intersect administration and milestone-based disbursement controls
request.what: Daedalus Wallet Maintenance and Improvements 2026-2027 delivered by Se7en Labs, Inc.

claims.claim: Daedalus is described as Cardano's only full-node desktop wallet, running an embedded Cardano node and deriving wallet and governance data directly from chain without third-party APIs or trusted backends.

Daedalus is open-source under Apache License 2.0, and all funded outputs including source code, build tooling, documentation, and release artifacts are presented as public assets forkable by anyone under that license.

Opt-in telemetry reportedly shows approximately 4,000 monthly active Daedalus users, while the proposer asserts the true count is meaningfully higher because privacy-conscious full-node users are less likely to opt in.

Se7en Labs says it assumed responsibility for Daedalus under an IOG contract in January 2026 and shipped Mithril Snapshot Bootstrap, UTxO-HD/LSM backend integration, native Apple Silicon builds, the drt release CLI, and Nix build modernization.

The proposal commits to maintain Daedalus compatibility through upcoming protocol changes, with stable releases at least 2 weeks before each mainnet hard fork and cardano-node no more than 2 major versions behind mainnet recommendation.
The proposal requests 1,785,333 ADA, consisting of 1,666,667 ADA for team labor, 33,333 ADA for test hardware, 33,333 ADA for financial audit, and 52,000 ADA for Intersect budget administration.
The proposer states any unspent labor, hardware, and audit budget at contract close will be returned to the treasury.

The proposal states Intersect will administer funds, verify milestones, hold funds in a dedicated auditable account, and disburse monthly against verified work using a treasury management smart contract framework developed by Sundae Labs.
The requested amount is asserted not to breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.

The risk register identifies ADA/USD volatility, upstream cardano-node API changes, Leios/Peras complexity, platform dependency changes, and team continuity as risks, with mitigations including prompt conversion to USD-backed stablecoins, time-and-materials scope absorption, IOG relationships, maintained signing arrangements, and documented tooling.

summary: The proposal seeks 1,785,333 ADA for a time-and-materials public-good maintenance and improvement program for Daedalus, emphasizing protocol compatibility, full-node wallet security, open-source outputs, hardware wallet support, CIP-30, Japanese localisation, support, and Intersect-administered oversight.
